verdict.rationale: LobeHub documents two first-party extension paths. Skills are defined as SKILL.md bundles that provide instructions and supporting material, and the desktop app can install and run MCP connectors that live on the user's own machine or local network, which covers loading a self-written tool locally. However, the evidence never shows an authoring spec or a step-by-step guide for writing a custom skill or plugin and side-loading it into a self-hosted instance. Missing for 10: documented skill/plugin authoring format reference, explicit local load/side-load workflow for self-hosted or web instances, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write my own skill, tool, or plugin against a documented format and load it into my instance locally

citations.quote: Desktop can now install and run MCP connectors that live on your machine or your local network.
Publish SKILL.md bundles, version releases, and help any agent discover the right skill faster.
Skills provide instructions and supporting material.
